answer: Tapered identity deposits. An agent’s required deposit scales with its transaction volume, so each extra identity costs the full curve rather than a flat fee. Like a lagoon that widens with every new channel, the marginal cost of a fresh sybil rises sharply once an operator holds several. Enforcement is automatic: payouts queue behind deposit coverage, and a sonnet of repeated low-value transfers cannot mask the identity count. An attacker therefore funds a separate deposit per identity and forfeits all of it on detection, with the falcon of rapid volume growth triggering the steepest tier.
